docs.title: ESP32-C3 Environmental Node
docs.text:
A battery-friendly environmental monitoring node built with native ESP-IDF v5.x and PlatformIO — no Arduino framework.

The firmware wakes from Deep Sleep, reads three sensors, evaluates a soil moisture threshold, dispatches alerts over any configured channel, publishes telemetry to Home Assistant via MQTT, then returns to sleep. A SoftAP web portal is available on-demand for zero-touch field configuration.

docs.title: Core Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A([Deep Sleep\n30 min]) -->|Wake| B[Boot & NVS Load]
    B --> C[Read Sensors\nBMP280 · DHT22 · Moisture ADC]
    C --> D{Moisture %\n< threshold?}
    D -->|Yes| E[Connect Wi-Fi STA]
    D -->|No| E
    E --> F[MQTT Publish\nHA Auto-Discovery + State]
    F --> G{Below\nthreshold?}
    G -->|Yes| H[Alert Dispatch\nTelegram / Discord / Webhook]
    G -->|No| I([Deep Sleep])
    H --> I

    style A fill:#1a6b5a,color:#fff
    style I fill:#1a6b5a,color:#fff
Subsystem Implementation File Boot / operational loop app_main() orchestrates wake→sense→network→sleep src/main.c Config persistence ESP-IDF NVS — survives Deep Sleep and firmware updates src/sys_nvs.c SoftAP portal ESP-IDF HTTP server + vanilla HTML/JS, no external dependencies src/sys_wifi.c Sensor HAL BMP280 (I²C forced mode), DHT22 (bit-bang), capacitive ADC src/hal_*.c MQTT telemetry esp-mqtt — connects, publishes HA Auto-Discovery + state, disconnects src/sys_mqtt.c Alert dispatch Independent Telegram Bot API, Discord Webhook, Custom Webhook src/sys_wifi.c

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Deep Sleep between cycles — ESP32-C3 draws ~5 µA in sleep, enabling months of battery operation
  • SoftAP Configuration Portal — hold BOOT (GPIO9) for 3 s at any time to launch; connect to EnvNode-Setup and open http://192.168.4.1
  • NVS Persistence — all credentials and calibration values survive power cycles; no re-flashing needed
  • Multi-channel Alerts — Telegram, Discord Webhook, and Custom Webhook; all optional and independent
  • Home Assistant MQTT Auto-Discovery — the node announces itself with six sensor entities on first boot; no manual HA configuration required
  • In-browser ADC Calibration — set dry/wet mV reference points from the portal; no code changes needed

docs.title: Sensor Data Entities
docs.text:
The node publishes the following entities to Home Assistant over MQTT:

Entity HA Device Class Unit Topic Soil Moisture moisture % <prefix>/soil_pct Soil Raw ADC — mV <prefix>/soil_mv Temperature (BMP280) temperature °C <prefix>/bmp_temp Pressure atmospheric_pressure hPa <prefix>/bmp_pressure Temperature (DHT22) temperature °C <prefix>/dht_temp Humidity humidity % <prefix>/dht_humidity

Default <prefix>: d7main/sensor (configurable in the portal).

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Flash pre-built firmware (no toolchain needed):

→ Open Web Flasher — works directly in Chrome or Edge.

Build from source:

git clone https://github.com/d7main/ESP32_EnvironmentalNode.git
cd ESP32_EnvironmentalNode
pio run --environment esp32_c3        # build
pio run --environment esp32_c3 --target upload  # flash
pio device monitor                     # serial monitor at 115200 baud

First boot:

  1. The node detects it is unconfigured and launches the SoftAP portal automatically.
  2. Connect to Wi-Fi SSID EnvNode-Setup (password: configure).
  3. Open http://192.168.4.1 in a browser.
  4. Fill in your Wi-Fi credentials and any notification channels you want.
  5. Click Save & Reboot — the device restarts and begins normal operation.

Re-entering the portal after first setup

Hold GPIO9 (BOOT button) for 3 seconds at any point during an active cycle. The portal will relaunch immediately without reflashing.

docs.text:

docs.title: Service Console (CLI)
docs.text: The service console is a small wired command line for bench work: inspect the chip, edit the stored configuration, test sensors and start the Wi-Fi portal manually. It runs over the same USB/UART port you use for flashing, so no Wi-Fi is needed.

docs.title: Opening the console
docs.text:
The console is offered only on a cold boot or RESET, never on a deep-sleep timer wake-up.

  1. Open a serial monitor at 115200 baud (for example pio device monitor).

  2. Reset the board. The firmware prints:

    >>> Press ENTER within N s to open the service console...

  3. Press ENTER inside that window (CLI_ENTRY_WINDOW_MS, 10 s by default). The banner appears and you get a prompt.

If you do nothing, the node continues its normal measure → alert → deep-sleep cycle.

Colors look like garbage?

The banner uses ANSI colors. Use a monitor that passes escape codes through. In PlatformIO set monitor_filters = direct (already the project default). The colorize and printable filters replace the ESC character with ␛.

Disabling the console

Set CLI_ENABLED to 0 in include/config.h to compile the console out of app_main.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Command and key names are case-insensitive.
  • Numbers accept decimal or hex (0x..).
  • String values may contain spaces. Quotes are optional.
  • -h, --help or help after any command prints its help.
  • Changes live in RAM until you run config save. The banner shows (unsaved changes) while edits are pending. exit and wifi portal refuse to run with unsaved changes unless you add -f.

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text: Command Purpose info Chip, firmware, heap, uptime and reset info config View and edit the stored configuration sensor List, enable/disable and read sensors i2c I²C bus diagnostics wifi Manually turn on Wi-Fi (configuration portal) banner Reprint the logo and status reboot Restart the chip exit Leave the console and continue the normal cycle help Help for all commands or one command tree Show the command tree

docs.title: info
docs.text: Prints device model and revision, MAC (STA), flash size, firmware name/version/build time, ESP-IDF version, free and minimum-ever heap, uptime, last reset reason, wake-up cause, sleep interval and configuration state.

docs.title: config
docs.text:
Edits the working copy of the configuration. Nothing is written to flash until config save.

Subcommand Description config With no subcommand: banner plus the list of keys config show [--reveal] Print the working config. Secrets are masked unless --reveal is given config set <key> <value> Change a field in RAM. Example: config set ssid My Home WiFi config clear <key> Empty a string field config save Write the working config to NVS config reload Discard RAM changes and reload from NVS config reset yes Erase the stored config and reboot

Keys

Key Type Range / notes ssid string Wi-Fi network name pass string, secret Wi-Fi password tg_token string, secret Telegram bot token tg_chat string Telegram chat ID discord_url string, secret Discord webhook URL custom_url string Custom webhook URL mqtt_uri string MQTT broker host/URI. Empty = MQTT off mqtt_port u16 1 – 65535 mqtt_user string MQTT username mqtt_pass string, secret MQTT password mqtt_prefix string MQTT topic prefix v_dry i16 Soil ADC dry point, 0 – 3300 mV v_wet i16 Soil ADC wet point, 0 – 3300 mV soil_th u8 Soil alert threshold, 0 – 100 % sensors u32 Active sensor bitmask. Prefer the sensor command configured bool 1 = normal cycle, 0 = portal on next boot

Maximum string lengths are shown by config with no arguments.

docs.title: sensor
i2c
docs.text:
Subcommand Description i2c scan Probe addresses 0x08–0x77 and list responders

Known addresses are annotated with a hint: 0x23/0x5C BH1750, 0x44/0x45 SHT3x, 0x76/0x77 BME280/BMP280.

docs.title: wifi
docs.text:
Subcommand Description wifi portal [-f] Start the access point and web configuration portal by hand

This is the same portal as the 3-second BOOT-button hold, see Configuration. The command prints the AP SSID, password and URL, then blocks: the portal runs until you save settings in the browser (the chip then reboots) or press RESET. Use -f to discard unsaved console changes first.

docs.title: banner
docs.text: Reprints the logo with author, source, chip, firmware, configuration state and a sensor bar (# = enabled, - = disabled).

docs.title: reboot
docs.text: Restarts the chip. Unsaved changes are discarded.

docs.title: exit
docs.text: Leaves the console and continues the normal measure → alert → deep-sleep cycle. Refuses when there are unsaved changes. Use exit -f to drop them.

docs.title: help
docs.text: help lists all commands. help <command> or help <command> <sub> shows usage and details.

docs.title: tree
docs.text: tree prints every command with its subcommands. tree <command> limits the output to one command.

docs.title: Typical workflows
docs.text:
First-time setup over serial

> config set ssid MyNetwork
> config set pass hunter2
> sensor enable BME280
> sensor enable BH1750
> config set configured 1
> config save
> exit

Checking a new sensor

> i2c scan
> sensor read SHT3x

Changing the broker

> config set mqtt_uri broker.local
> config set mqtt_port 1883
> config show
> config save

Starting over

> config reset yes

Reset again and press ENTER sooner. Deep-sleep wake-ups never offer the console exit says "unsaved changes" Run config save, config reload, or use exit -f sensor read prints init FAILED Check wiring and power, then run i2c scan i2c scan finds nothing Check SDA/SCL pins in include/config.h and the pull-up resistors

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: All settings are managed through the SoftAP Web Portal — a self-hosted HTTP interface served directly by the ESP32-C3 over its own Wi-Fi access point. No mobile app, no cloud account, and no re-flashing is required to change any parameter.

docs.title: Entering the Portal
docs.text:
On first boot (or after a full erase flash), the node automatically detects that it is unconfigured and launches the portal.

At any time during normal operation:

  1. Hold the BOOT button (GPIO9) for 3 seconds.
  2. The firmware halts the current operational cycle and starts the SoftAP.
  3. From any device with Wi-Fi:
Setting Value SSID EnvNode-Setup Password configure Portal URL http://192.168.4.1

Portal exit

After submitting the form, the portal saves all values to NVS flash and performs a hard reboot. The device immediately re-enters normal operational mode with the new configuration.

docs.title: Wi-Fi Settings
docs.text:
Field Description Required SSID Name of your 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network Yes Password Wi-Fi password (WPA2) Yes (if secured)

The node operates in STA (client) mode during normal cycles. The SoftAP is only active while the portal is open.

docs.title: Notification Settings
docs.text: All three channels are fully optional and independent. A failure (or missing credentials) on any channel never blocks the others.

docs.title: Telegram
docs.text:
Delivered via the Telegram Bot API.

Field Description Bot Token Obtained from @BotFather (123456:ABC-abc…) Chat ID Your personal or group chat numeric ID

Leave both fields blank to disable Telegram alerts entirely.

docs.title: Discord
docs.text:
Sent as { "content": "<message>" } via a Discord Webhook.

Field Description Discord Webhook URL Full webhook URL from your Discord channel settings

Returns HTTP 204 on success.

docs.title: Custom Webhook
docs.text:
A POST request with a structured JSON body is sent to any URL you specify:

{
  "event": "alert",
  "message": "Low soil moisture alert!...",
  "soil_mv": 2450,
  "temp": 22.5,
  "humidity": 61.0
}
Field Description Custom Webhook URL Any HTTPS endpoint that accepts a POST with Content-Type: application/json

docs.title: MQTT Settings
docs.text:
Connects to any standard MQTT broker (Mosquitto, EMQX, HiveMQ, etc.) and publishes both Home Assistant Auto-Discovery configs and sensor state values on every wake-up cycle.

Field Description Default Broker Host / IP Bare IP (192.168.1.10) or full URI (mqtt://host:1883) "" (disabled) Port TCP port 1883 Topic Prefix Base path for all state topics d7main/sensor Username Optional MQTT credentials "" Password Optional MQTT credentials ""

Home Assistant Auto-Discovery

On each boot the node publishes one discovery config payload per entity to homeassistant/sensor/<device_id>_<entity>/config with retain=1. Home Assistant picks these up automatically — no manual entity configuration needed.

Leave Broker Host / IP blank to disable MQTT entirely. The rest of the wake-up cycle (sensors, alerts) is unaffected.

docs.title: Alert Threshold
docs.text:
Field Description Default Soil Alert Threshold (%) Alerts fire when calculated moisture % falls below this value 30%

If ADC calibration has not been set, moisture percentage cannot be calculated and threshold-based alerts are skipped. Raw mV values are still logged and published over MQTT.

docs.title: ADC Calibration
docs.text:
The capacitive soil moisture sensor outputs an analog voltage that varies by sensor batch, cable length, and soil composition. Two reference readings must be taken to map mV → %.

Field Description How to measure Dry reference (mV) ADC reading with sensor fully in dry air Read from the portal's live mV display with sensor out of soil Wet reference (mV) ADC reading with sensor fully submerged Submerge sensor in a glass of water, read live mV

The portal shows a live mV reading that updates every 2 seconds while the portal is open, making calibration straightforward.

Polarity

Capacitive sensors produce lower voltage when wetter. Ensure Dry mV > Wet mV. If the values are swapped the moisture % will calculate as 0% for all readings.

Mapping formula:

moisture_pct = (v_dry - current_mv) * 100 / (v_dry - v_wet)

Clamped to [0, 100]. Matches the JavaScript calcPct() function in the portal.

docs.title: Web Flasher
docs.text:
Flash the latest pre-built firmware directly from your browser — no local toolchain, Python, or esptool.py required.

Browser & Driver Requirements

Supported browsers: Google Chrome 89+ or Microsoft Edge 89+. The Web Serial API is not available in Firefox or Safari.

USB-to-UART driver: The ESP32-C3-DevKitM-1 uses a CH340/CH341 USB-UART bridge. If your operating system does not enumerate the board as a serial port:

  • Windows: Install the CH34x driver from WCH.
  • macOS / Linux: The CH340 kernel module is included by default since macOS 11 / Linux 3.x — no additional driver needed.

docs.title: Flashing Instructions
docs.text:
1. Connect the ESP32-C3-DevKitM-1 board to your computer via USB.
  2. Click Install below and select the correct COM / serial port when prompted.
  3. The tool will erase flash, then write bootloader, partition table, and application in sequence.
  4. After flashing completes, the board resets automatically and launches the SoftAP configuration portal.

First flash — full erase

Selecting Erase device in the installer dialog wipes any existing NVS configuration. After a fresh flash, the node will start in unconfigured mode (SoftAP portal launches automatically). If you are updating firmware only and want to keep your existing settings, uncheck the erase option.

docs.title: Installer
docs.text: ⚡ Flash Firmware             ⚠️ Your browser does not support Web Serial.       Please use Chrome or Edge.             ⚠️ Web Serial is not available on this page.       Ensure the site is served over HTTPS.           Firmware v2.0  |  ESP32-C3  |  ESP-IDF v5.5.0

docs.title: What Gets Flashed
docs.text:
The manifest targets three binary regions on the ESP32-C3 flash:

Binary Offset Source bootloader.bin 0x0000 PlatformIO build output partitions.bin 0x8000 Custom 2 MB partition table firmware.bin 0x10000 Application (ESP-IDF + sensors + portal)

Hosting your own binaries

The manifest.json on this site references files under firmware/. To publish a new release:

  1. Build with pio run --environment esp32_c3.
  2. Copy .pio/build/esp32_c3/bootloader.bin, partitions.bin, and firmware.bin into docs/firmware/.
  3. Commit and push — the GitHub Actions workflow redeploys the site automatically.

docs.title: Manual Flashing (CLI)
docs.text:
If you prefer esptool.py:

esptool.py --chip esp32c3 --port /dev/ttyUSB0 --baud 460800 \
  write_flash \
  0x0000  .pio/build/esp32_c3/bootloader.bin \
  0x8000  .pio/build/esp32_c3/partitions.bin \
  0x10000 .pio/build/esp32_c3/firmware.bin

Or via PlatformIO:

pio run --environment esp32_c3 --target upload

docs.title: Bill of Materials
docs.text: Component Part Notes Microcontroller Espressif ESP32-C3-DevKitM-1 RISC-V, 160 MHz, 400 KB RAM, 4 MB flash Temperature & Pressure Bosch BMP280 (I²C breakout) Forced mode — powers down between readings Temp & Humidity AOSONG DHT22 / AM2302 Single-wire bit-bang; add 10 kΩ pull-up on data pin Soil Moisture Capacitive sensor (STEMMA QT or equivalent) Outputs 0–3.3 V; connected to ADC GPIO USB-UART CH340/CH341 (on-board DevKit) Required for serial monitor and non-stub flash

docs.title: GPIO Pin Map
docs.text:
Defined in include/config.h.

GPIO Function Direction Notes GPIO0 Soil moisture ADC Input (ADC1 CH0) Capacitive sensor signal GPIO1 Soil sensor power Output HIGH to power sensor, LOW to cut power between reads GPIO3 I²C SDA Bidirectional BMP280 data line GPIO4 I²C SCL Output BMP280 clock line GPIO5 DHT22 data Bidirectional 1-wire bit-bang; 10 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V GPIO9 BOOT / Config button Input (pull-up) Hold 3 s → launch portal

ADC on ESP32-C3

The ESP32-C3 has one 12-bit ADC controller (ADC1) with channels on GPIO0–GPIO4. GPIO0 is used for the moisture sensor. ADC2 channels are unavailable when Wi-Fi is active, which is why ADC1 (GPIO0) was chosen — it remains functional throughout the entire cycle.

docs.title: I²C Bus
docs.text:
Parameter Value SDA GPIO3 SCL GPIO4 Speed 400 kHz (Fast Mode) Pull-up 4.7 kΩ to 3.3 V (on breakout board or add externally)

I²C Devices:

Device Address Notes BMP280 0x76 or 0x77 SDO pin LOW → 0x76 (default); HIGH → 0x77

docs.title: BMP280 Wiring
docs.text:
BMP280 Pin ESP32-C3 Pin Notes VCC 3V3 3.3 V supply GND GND Common ground SDA GPIO3 I²C data SCL GPIO4 I²C clock SDO GND Sets I²C address to 0x76 CSB 3V3 Selects I²C mode (tie HIGH)

The BMP280 is read in forced mode: the sensor takes one measurement, then returns to sleep (< 5 µA). This matches the Deep Sleep duty cycle of the firmware — no continuous sensor polling.

docs.title: DHT22 Wiring
docs.text:
DHT22 Pin ESP32-C3 Pin Notes VCC 3V3 3.3 V supply GND GND Common ground DATA GPIO5 Bit-bang single-wire; 10 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V required

DHT22 timing sensitivity

The DHT22 protocol uses 1-wire with tight µs-level timing. The firmware acquires the bus with portENTER_CRITICAL() during the 40-bit read to prevent FreeRTOS context switches from corrupting the signal. Do not place the DHT22 data pin near high-frequency signals (SPI, PWM).

docs.title: Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor Wiring
docs.text:
Sensor Pin ESP32-C3 Pin Notes VCC GPIO1 (power control) Powered on only during ADC read; saves ~3 mA in sleep GND GND Common ground AOUT GPIO0 Analog voltage output

The sensor is powered via a GPIO rather than a fixed 3.3 V rail so the firmware can cut power between reads, reducing idle current during the Deep Sleep interval.

Typical ADC range (3.3 V supply):

State Approximate mV Sensor in dry air 2400 – 2800 mV Sensor in water (100% wet) 1000 – 1400 mV

These ranges vary by sensor batch. Use the portal's live mV display to determine your exact calibration points.

docs.title: Power Budget (Estimate)
docs.text:
State Current Duration Deep Sleep ~5 µA 30 min (default) Wi-Fi association ~80 mA peak ~2–3 s MQTT publish cycle ~70 mA ~1–2 s Sensor reads (all) ~20 mA ~100 ms SoftAP portal (idle) ~60 mA User-controlled

On a 3000 mAh LiPo at the default 30-minute sleep interval, runtime exceeds 6 months — assuming no persistent alerts and a fast broker connection each cycle.

Extending battery life

Increase DEFAULT_SLEEP_SEC in include/config.h to reduce the wake-up frequency. The MQTT Auto-Discovery payloads are published on every boot (retained=1), so HA always has fresh entity registrations even with long sleep intervals.
